title: ARP4754B — Guidelines for Development of Civil Aircraft and Systems
authors: SAE International (S-18 Aircraft and Systems Development and Safety Assessment Committee)
ident: SAE ARP4754B (Rev. B, issued 2023-12-20; supersedes ARP4754A 2010-12-21; original ARP4754 issued 1996-11)
evidence: Live page saemobilus.sae.org/content/arp4754b (SAE's own platform), title 'ARP4754B: Guidelines for Development of Civil Aircraft and Systems - Recommended Practice'; page confirms revision dates 'Issued November 1996', rev A 2010-12-21, rev B 2023-12-20.
note: The aircraft/system-level requirements-capture process (Sections on planning and system requirements) is the aerospace field's name for the needs stage: it produces the aircraft- and system-level functional/safety requirements that DO-178C software requirements (largely handwritten C at DAL A/B) are derived from and traced to. Also serves obligations via Development Assurance Level assignment from functional hazard assessment; tagged both.

title: Automotive SPICE Process Assessment Model, v4.0 — SYS.1 Requirements Elicitation
authors: VDA QMC Working Group 13 (VDA Quality Management Center, with intacs)
ident: Automotive SPICE PAM v4.0, Version 4.0, dated 2023-11-29, status 'Released', PUBLIC
evidence: Fetched the official PDF from vda-qmc.de/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Automotive-SPICE-PAM-v40.pdf and extracted text live. Title page: 'Automotive SPICE Process Assessment / Reference Model, VDA Working Group 13, 4.0, 2023-11-29, Released'. Process SYS.1 'Requirements Elicitation' purpose: 'The purpose is to gather, analyze, and track evolving stakeholder needs and requirements throughout the lifecycle of the product and/or service to establish a set of agreed requirements.' BP1: 'Obtain stakeholder expectations and requests ... through direct solicitation of stakeholder input ...'.
note: SYS.1 is the automotive industry's own name for the needs stage, sitting immediately upstream of SYS.2 (System Requirements Analysis) and SWE.1 (Software Requirements Analysis) — the process most automotive ECU software (still majority handwritten C) is assessed against. This is the strongest direct hit for the hand-c x needs cell: same vocabulary problem the mission flags ("stakeholder needs" rather than the mission's own term), found by searching the field's own name for it.

authors: ECSS Secretariat (European Cooperation for Space Standardization)

title: IEC 62366-1:2015 — Medical devices — Part 1: Application of usability engineering to medical devices
evidence: Live page iso.org/standard/63179.html, title confirmed exactly: 'IEC 62366-1:2015 - Medical devices — Part 1: Application of usability engineering to medical devices'.
note: Requires manufacturers to define 'user needs', 'use specification' and 'user interface specification' before deriving requirements; these feed the software requirements and safety classification of IEC 62304 (held as membership 'iec62304'), whose Class B/C firmware for devices such as infusion pumps and pacemakers is overwhelmingly handwritten C. The medical-device field's name for the needs stage.

title: General Principles of Software Validation; Final Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff
authors: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Center for Devices and Radiological Health / Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research
evidence: Live FDA page (fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/general-principles-software-validation) confirmed exact title 'General Principles of Software Validation Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff', issuing date January 2002, docket FDA-1997-D-0029.
note: Codifies the medical-device V-model (user needs -> design input -> verification/validation) that regulators expect embedded medical-device software (largely handwritten C) to trace back to; the canonical U.S. regulatory articulation of the needs->requirements chain for this domain.
